amendments.what: iPhone: a fresh number taken through the front Subscribe door goes STRAIGHT to About you — the trial-or-subscribe window never appears. WALK-A-021 asked for the offer once per session; the web has `sessionStorage`, which dies with the tab, but the phone's `storage` is permanent, so the flag was written to the device for good. Once anyone answered that window on a phone, no teacher on that phone was ever offered the free trial again. A revenue-side bug, not a cosmetic one. ✓ iPhone re-walk 2026-09-20: green.
amendments.fix: PHONE: the flag is a module variable — it lives exactly as long as the app process, which is what 'session' means here — and the stale persisted key is cleared on mount so devices that already took it recover. Backing out of the window (WALK-A-042) resets it too.

amendments.title: Pinned feet sit under the Android navigation bar
amendments.what: Pixel 7, with the emulator switched to 3-button navigation: the sign-in screen's foot sits straight under ◁ ◯ ▢, so 'Already have an ID? Sign in' cannot be pressed — the press lands on the system bar. Edge-to-edge is mandatory from Android 16, so the app owns that space and must give the bar its room. The gesture pill is thin enough that every foot LOOKED right until the walk switched navigation modes; a great many Android teachers use the three buttons.
amendments.fix: PHONE: every pinned foot adds the safe-area bottom inset — login's Wrap, the subscribe wizard's three feet, the Agreement's foot, and first-run's scroll tail. The bottom nav already did this.

amendments.title: Android: the keypad covers the sign-in screen's pinned foot
amendments.what: Pixel 7 dev build: with the OTP keypad up, the sign-in screen's pinned foot stayed at the bottom of the screen and the keys drew over it, so the app's own '← Back' could not be seen or pressed. The KeyboardAvoidingView lifted on iOS only — `undefined` on Android was right while the window resized for the keypad, but under mandatory edge-to-edge the IME simply draws over the app and nothing resizes. (Not to be confused with Android replacing ◁ with the ⌄ dismiss-keyboard chevron while the IME is open — that is the system's own behaviour and correct.)
amendments.fix: PHONE: the sign-in Wrap lifts on both surfaces (behavior="padding"), so the foot rides the keyboard.

amendments.title: A returning subscriber is told she used a free trial she never had
amendments.what: Pixel 7: 9000000004 took the Free-to-try door and landed in the subscribe wizard under 'This mobile number has already used its free trial. Subscribe to keep using Meyy.' The ledger is right to refuse — api/main.py records `spent=(ent_before.status != "trial")`, so an erased PAID account cannot come back on a free trial, which stops subscribe-cancel-delete-rejoin farming. But 04's entry reads chapters_used: 0. She never had a trial; she paid. The sentence states something untrue about her own history at the moment she is being asked to pay again. FOUNDER'S CALL on the wording; the rule itself is sound and should not change. FOUNDER (2026-09-21): the quota belongs to the number and is consumed by chapters USED, notwithstanding a direct subscription — one consistent rule for everyone, on all three surfaces.
amendments.fix: SERVER (all surfaces at once): erasure records only the chapters actually used — `note_erased(user_id, real_used)`, no paid⇒spent. And the trial-usage record now SURVIVES the purchase that supersedes the trial (manual_billing_provider carried `trial_chapters` only when the prior was not a trial, so a teacher who tried two chapters then subscribed came back to all three). Inert while subscribed: every gate reading that list checks `status == "trial"` first. Two tests replace the old one.
